description: Build a monthly purchase-retention matrix for the ecommerce marketplace. A user's cohort is the UTC month of their first completed order. For each cohort and each month_offset (0 = cohort month, 1 = next calendar month, ...), count distinct users of the cohort who placed at least one completed order in that month, and compute retention_rate = active_users / cohort_size. Only emit (cohort, offset) pairs with at least one active user. Output columns: cohort_month (DATE), month_offset (INT64), cohort_size (INT64), active_users (INT64), retention_rate (FLOAT64, 4 decimals). Sort by cohort_month, month_offset.

registered_at.description: Registration time (not used for the cohort)

edge_cases: User 3's first order was cancelled, so their cohort is February (first COMPLETED order)
Two orders in the same month count the user once
Month offset is a calendar-month difference (Jan 31 to Mar 1 is offset 2), not days / 30
cohort_size is constant across offsets of a cohort
common_failure_modes: FM3: COUNT(*) instead of COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) inflates active_users for repeat buyers
FM2: Computing the offset as DATE_DIFF(days) / 30 misplaces orders near month boundaries
FM3: Deriving cohort_size from the offset-level group instead of the cohort makes every retention_rate 1.0
